answer: A raven drawn from a shared randomness beacon audits a random slice of nodes, and any duplicate attestation triggers a ripple of slashed stake across the cluster. At dawn each epoch, an agent must post a bond tied to a verified hardware or biometric attestation, renewing it daily so a single operator can't cheaply spin up thousands of identities. Forging N sybils therefore costs N real bonds plus forfeited collateral, making mass fakery economically irrational. From qwe0006's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
